title: Pulse‑meter suite: robust tokens/sec & p95 regression detection harness
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a resilient, reproducible microbenchmark harness (Pulse‑meter) that measures end‑to‑end tokens/sec and p95 latency across core models and common request shapes. The suite will: 1) provide multi‑model, multi‑sequence workload profiles (short chat turns, long completions, multi‑context retrieval patterns), 2) include KV‑cache warm/warmless variants, 3) run synthetic replay and sampled production‑traffic replays, 4) surface time‑series of tokens/sec and p95 with rolling windows and statistical baselines, and 5) integrate automated regression detection and PagerDuty/Slack alerts for sustained degradations. Deliverables: harness code, CI jobs, dashboard in Console for the last 90 days, automated regression rule set, and a lightweight runbook for investigating noisy signals.
acceptance_criteria: Daily CI runs produce a stable baseline JSON artifact for each core model and workload profile
Regression rule fires when 24h rolling p95 increases by >10% or tokens/sec median drops by >7% compared to baseline
Benchmarks support KV cache variants (cold, prewarmed, shared) and document how each is exercised
Produced metrics are ingested into the Console dashboard (90d retention) and link to the harness run artifacts
Integration tests validate end‑to‑end: harness -> metrics -> alerting -> Ops notification (test PagerDuty trigger)
metrics: tokens_per_sec: median, 75th, 95th over sliding 1h and 24h windows
p95_latency_ms: sampled per request and aggregated similarly
variance_index: coefficient of variation for tokens/sec (target < 0.15 for stable runs)
regression_flag: boolean with reason and delta percent
updates: 2025-02-11 - Aisha Raman: Scoped initial profiles and chose three canonical workloads (chat_short, completion_long, retrieval_combo). Confluence: /confluence/redwood/pulse-meter-spec (draft)

2025-02-18 - Liam Ortega: Prototype harness implemented (python) that drives our local runner and emits protobuf/JSON artifacts. Initial runs on dev-gpu-04 show tokens/sec baseline for model-rw-1 of 8.3k tok/s (short workload). PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pulse-meter/pull/7

2025-02-24 - Performance spike observed in long completion profile during warm cache tests; root cause traced to kernel scheduling changes in runtime-1.19. Opened ENG-12157 to track scheduling follow-up. Temporary mitigation: cap concurrency for long profiles in CI runs
2025-03-01 - Added rolling‑window p95 computation (24h/1h) and regression detector prototype (statsd exporter + alert rules). Created dashboard draft and linked to runtime‑1.20 release notes

2025-03-03 - Design review with SRE and Console PM. Agreed on alert thresholds and synthetic vs replay sample ratio (80% synthetic, 20% replay). Blocker: need stabilized GPU CI pool for repeatable long runs (tracking ENG-990210). Next: harden artifact storage and add PR gating job.
notes: Tradeoffs: prioritized repeatability and low noise over absolute production fidelity; opted for hybrid synthetic/replay approach to balance cost and signal quality.
Decision: perform KV warm‑up using deterministic prefix sequences to avoid noisy cache state between runs.
Future: explore embedding sampling to correlate quality regressions with perf regressions (separate ticket).
